chunks.heading: Introduction
chunks.text:
(as on 06.05.2025)




Heavy Rainfall accompanied with thunderstorm, lightning & squally/gusty winds likely over Gujarat state and southwest Rajasthan during 05th-08th May & over Uttarakhand during 6th-7th May 2025. Heavy Rainfall accompanied with thunderstorm & lightning likely over northeast India during 06th to 08th May, 2025. Inputs Situation a. Water Reservoir Status: As on 01st May 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 60.68 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 33% of total live storage capacity (182.37 BCM).The current year's storage is nearly 117 percent of last year's storage and 114 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. b. Groundwater Levels: Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014– 2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024. c. Seeds and Fertilizers: For Rabi 2024-25, certified seed availability is 337.98 lakh quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 6. Pests & Diseases: The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level. 7. chunks.heading: Details of each Segment
chunks.text:
During the week (24 – 30 April 2025), lower rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 34%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01th Mar to 30th April 2025) is lower than LPA by 15%.
Rainfall Forecast: 01 May – 07 May 2025 The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over central Pakistan adjoining Punjab & northwest Rajasthan in lower to upper tropospheric levels. Rainfall accompanied with thunderstorms, lightning, Hailstorms, squally/gusty winds likely to continue over Northwest India during next 7 days; over central India till 07th and decrease in intensity thereafter. Heavy Rainfall accompanied with thunderstorm, lightning & squally/gusty winds likely over Gujarat state and southwest Rajasthan during 05th-08th May & over Uttarakhand during 6th-7th May 2025. Heavy Rainfall accompanied with thunderstorm & lightning likely over northeast India during 06th to 08th May, 2025. 08 May – 14 May 2025 Under the influence of western disturbances, scattered to fairly widespread rainfall with thunderstorm is likely over Western Himalayan Region; isolated to scattered over plains of northwest India during some/many days of the week. Due to trough/cyclonic circulations over central & south Peninsular India, light/moderate scattered to fairly widespread rainfall along with thunderstorm & lightening are likely over central & south Peninsular India during many days of the week. Overall, normal to above normal rainfall along with thunderstorm & lightening are likely over northwest, Central and South Peninsular India; below normal over east & northeast
India during the week.

chunks.heading: 2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX
chunks.text:
Temperature Forecast : Maximum Temperature Week 1 (02 May – 08 May): No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over Northwest India & Central India during next 4 days and rise by 2-3°C thereafter for subsequent 4 days.
No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over West India during next 3 days and rise by 3-5°C thereafter for subsequent 4 days. Gradual fall in maximum temperature likely over West India by 3-5°C during next 7 days. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country. Week 2 (09 May – 15 May): Maximum temperatures are likely to be above normal by 1-3°C over many parts of Western Himalayan Region and northeast India, over Odisha, Coastal Andhra Pradesh and coastal Tamil Nadu. These are likely to be near normal or below normal over rest parts of the country. Heat Wave forecast : Week 1(2nd to 8th May 2025) No chance of heatwave conditions over any parts of the country during the week. Week 2(9th to 15th May 2025) There is a low probability of heat wave conditions over /isolated pockets of Odisha and Coastal Andhra Pradesh during some days of the week.

chunks.heading: 3. RESERVOIR STORAGE (as on 01st May, 2025)
chunks.text:
Current live storage in 161 reservoirs was 60.68 BCM (33%) of total live capacity of 182.37 BCM. Table 1: For 161 major reservoirs of the country 120 reservoirs having storage more than 80% of normal storage. 24 reservoirs having storage 51% to 80%. 17 reservoirs having storage upto 50%. Source: CWC


Soil Moisture Observation Soil moisture during 26 April – 02 May2025 is better/similar to the average of the past 9 years in A.P, Karnataka, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Bihar, Jharkhand, W.B., U.P., Rajasthan, M.P, Haryana and Maharashtra. Whereas it is lower than average of past 9 years avg. in N.E. parts of the country. Summer Crops - Area coverage As on 02.05.2025, about 107.5 percent of the normal area has been sown under the Summer season crops. Rice: About 32.02 lakh ha area coverage under Summer Rice has been reported as compared to 28.57 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. Pulses: About 20.67 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 18.47 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. Oilseeds: About 9.51 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 9.23 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.
